To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the countrywide distribution of soil organic carbon stocks (SOCS) is moderately heterogeneous in Cameroon and can be accurately assessed at 100 m resolution using legacy soil data, machine learning models and spatial interpolation of the model residuals.

we have developed a countrywide estimate of soil organic carbon (SOC) stock at five depth layers in Cameroon using a national legacy soil database and machine learning models, and the SOC stocks are 5.7 ± 0.2 Pg C for the 0-100 cm soil depth.
We assessed the spatial distribution of soil organic carbon (SOC) stock in Cameroon using a national soil database with 1432 soil profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an accurate and reliable national SOCS inventory using legacy soil data in a data-scarce country.

the assessment of the countrywide spatial distribution of soil organic carbon stocks at five soil depth layers (0–15, 15–30, 30–100, 0–30 and 0–100 cm) in a tropical country, Cameroon, using a national legacy soil database (1432 soil profiles) and a set of environmental covariates.
the assessment of countrywide soil organic C stocks (SOCS) in Cameroon, using legacy soil data, environmental covariates and hybrid machine learning modelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RF model combined with OK interpolation of the residuals is the most appropriate approach for predicting SOCS at countrywide level, with the potential for upscaling to the global level.
the RF model with OK hybridization performed best for SOCS prediction in Cameroon, with an overall R2 of 0.77 and a mean absolute error of 7.2 Mg C ha 21.
the country wide estimates of soil organic C stocks in Cameroon are useful to set the national strategies for sustainable soil use management as well the global soil organic carbon stock inventories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hybrid machine learning modelling with spatial interpolation of the residual can be used to assess SOCS at a country scale with legacy soil data.
the hybrid modelling approach of random forest and ordinary kriging was the best model to estimate the countrywide distribution of soil organic carbon at different depths.
we were able to produce a national map of SOCS at 0.1 degree spatial resolution for Cameroon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
machine learning modelling combined with hybrid interpolation of residuals is an effective approach to assess the countrywide distribution of SOCS.
the RF model is a promising tool for predicting the SOCS distribution at national level.

the use of hybrid modelling approaches can improve the performance of machine learning models in predicting soil properties, and that the use of legacy data in machine learning modelling can improve prediction performance and reduce bias.
